# Discounted projective surface repair and scale-free concavity dissipation

This proves an auxiliary quantitative repair theorem. Its central
invariant is a LINEAR discounted-capacity constraint on the endpoint
coupling. It retains an exact nonnegative error measure, rather than
only its mass. The error is paid by the logarithmic Jensen gap of the
OLD coupling, with no inverse positive-floor coefficient. No OC
conclusion or vanishing of the actual entropy is asserted.

Dependencies, proved in the workspace, are:

* candidate 1dcb5bc1e68b837f;
* candidate 93c94ac2c5c85584;
* candidate 9764a982661d3ddc;
* measurable-assembly-of-density-repairs-root.md.

The restriction-of-the-existing-optimizer argument is the one audited
for contact-constrained-projective-surface-cell-repair-rate-geometry.md.

## 1. Data and theorem at one normal and parity

Use a finite lattice-complete compatible family of positive
 d-dimensional convex fibers, d>=1, its canonical convex hull C,
and actual normal-bundle surface measure eta. Coordinates are w=(z,x).
Let L=min_i A_i>0 on C for finitely many affine A_i. Thus L is
continuous concave, with ell=min_C L>0 and U=max_C L<infinity.
Let H be a common concave physical function and assume W=H_+/L^d
is bounded Borel on the actual and auxiliary surfaces. Set omega=W eta.
A normal-dependent H is permitted under the same assumptions.

Fix a good normal and one original integer parity class. Every
conditional surface law and auxiliary pair-average body is expressed
relative to ONE common normal reference. Let gamma_-,gamma_+<=omega
be endpoint measures of common mass m. Suppose pi_old couples them
with midpoints on the actual target support graph. All product endpoint
bases have integer midpoints, since they have the same parity.

Write b=(w_-+w_+)/2 and define continuous tuple functions

    V=(L(w_-)+L(w_+))/2,
    a=V/L(b),                      ell/U<=a<=1,
    delta_log=log L(b)-[log L(w_-)+log L(w_+)]/2>=0.

There is a coupling pi of the SAME marginals, retaining the actual
support graph, such that, with rho=b_#pi,

    b_#pi_old <=cx rho,                                      (1)
    D_pi:=b_#(a^d pi) <= omega.                              (2)

Define E_pi=b_#[(1-a^d)pi]. Then, as measures,

    rho=D_pi+E_pi,
    (rho-omega)_+ <= E_pi,
    rho <= (U/ell)^d omega.                                  (3)

Thus rho remains absolutely continuous with respect to the actual
weighted target surface. Put Delta_old=integral delta_log dpi_old.
For m>0,

    E_pi(total) <= m[1-exp(-d Delta_old/m)] <=d Delta_old.      (4)

If m=0 all laws and errors are zero. The floor occurs only in coarse
regularity (3), not in the exact constraint (2) or bound (4).

## 2. The exact discounted density envelope

At a good normal, the positive endpoint conditional laws have common
face dimension k and tangent space whenever their product midpoint
has actual target support contact. Write g_-,g_+,g_0 for their density
representatives and F_i=g_i H_i,+/L_i^d. For positive endpoint weights,
H_-,H_+>0, hence H_0>0 by concavity.

The common-affine weighted envelope uses the denominator only through
its three values and the inequality L_0<=(L_-+L_+)/2. Apply that algebra
with V as the middle denominator. It yields

    g_0 H_0/V^d >= N_k(F_-,F_+)        if k>0,
    g_0 H_0/V^d >= min(F_-,F_+)        if k=0,

where N_k(s,t)=[(s^(-1/k)+t^(-1/k))/2]^(-k). Multiplying by a^d gives

    F_0 >= a^d N_k(F_-,F_+)            if k>0,                (5)
    F_0 >= a^d min(F_-,F_+)            if k=0.

A zero endpoint weight gives a trivial zero lower envelope; no negative
power of zero is taken. For d=1 the faces are atoms, and the common
interval-normal atom mass, concavity of H, and V=(L_-+L_+)/2 prove the
atom assertion directly. No zero exponent is evaluated by a
positive-dimensional density formula.

## 3. Every constrained strong-surplus optimizer satisfies (2)

The support heights at the fixed normal have a finite concave PL roof
h_tilde(z)=min_j B_j(z), agreeing at each sampled base. On endpoint
support faces, actual target-graph contact is exactly

    J_h=h_tilde((z_-+z_+)/2)-[h_tilde(z_-)+h_tilde(z_+)]/2=0.

Let P be the compact convex class of fixed-marginal couplings on this
closed equality set. It is nonempty because it contains pi_old. There
is NO L-contact constraint.

Maximize a smooth globally strongly convex function of b over P.
Partition one maximizer pi_star by the least active roof plane B_j at
its OUTPUT. Both endpoints of its j-th restriction lie in the closed
convex cell {B_j=h_tilde}: the sum of their nonnegative endpoint plane
gaps is zero. Conversely every pair from this cell has J_h=0.

Any coupling of that restriction's endpoint marginals therefore remains
feasible. Global optimality makes the existing restriction an
UNRESTRICTED strong-surplus optimizer of its own marginals. The
supports of restricted marginals stay in the closed contact cell,
even if the assigned output tie part is not closed.

The inverse-endpoint-map proof applies to this optimizer ITSELF. Its
output law has density h on the intrinsic face, reconstructs one
endpoint tuple almost everywhere, and satisfies

    h<=N_k(F_-,F_+)                  if k>0,

with the atom/minimum version when k=0. Restricted endpoint marginals
remain bounded by the full weighted surface densities. Equation (5)
therefore gives a^d h<=F_0.

The ACTUAL restricted output laws are supported on disjoint canonical
output parts, including positive-mass ties. Their density bounds sum
to b_#(a^d pi_star)<=omega. We never rebuild the pieces or presume
that hypothetical replacements retain their original output labels.
No factor for the number of roof planes is introduced.

## 4. Convex order retains the exact linear discount constraint

Let D be the subset of P satisfying (2). It is convex and weakly
compact: for each nonnegative continuous output test f the defining
inequality is

    integral f(b) a^d dpi <= integral f domega,

which is linear and weakly closed because a^d is continuous bounded.
These tests characterize domination of finite measures on the compact
output space. Section 3 supplies nonemptiness of D.

For any finite globally convex physical test f, approximate f uniformly
on the compact output range by smooth strongly convex functions
(mollify on a neighborhood and add a vanishing positive quadratic).
Their maximizers over P lie in D and have objective at least the old
value. Compactness gives

    max_(pi in D) integral f(b)dpi >=integral f(b)dpi_old.     (6)

For a finite family of tests, their achievable expectation vectors over
D form a compact convex set. If this set missed the translate of the
nonnegative orthant above the old vector, strict separation would give
a nonnegative linear combination of the tests violating (6). Hence
all finitely many desired inequalities hold simultaneously. Compact
finite intersection produces pi in D satisfying (1).

The optimizers in Section 3 were over P, not over a class additionally
constrained by old-law convex order; that would invalidate the
unrestricted-piece argument.

Define D_pi,E_pi as in Section 1. Their sum is exactly rho. Since
D_pi<=omega, the minimal-majorant characterization of positive variation
gives (rho-omega)_+<=E_pi. Since a>=ell/U,
(ell/U)^d rho<=D_pi<=omega. This proves (3).

## 5. Scale-free logarithmic payment

Arithmetic-geometric mean gives

    log V>=[log L(w_-)+log L(w_+)]/2,
    -log a<=delta_log,
    1-a^d<=1-exp(-d delta_log)<=d delta_log.                (7)

The integrated logarithmic gap has the fixed-endpoint decomposition

    Delta(pi)=integral log L drho
          -(1/2) integral log L d(gamma_-+gamma_+).        (8)

To justify its convex-order comparison globally, set c=ell/2 and define

    psi(t)=-log t                  for t>=c,
    psi(t)=-log c-(t-c)/c          for t<c.

This is finite convex and decreasing on the real line. The globally
finite convex function max_i psi(A_i) agrees with -log L on C.
Equation (1), together with fixed endpoint marginals, now gives

    Delta(pi)<=Delta(pi_old)=Delta_old.                    (9)

Integrate (7), use concavity of s->1-exp(-d s) and Jensen for pi/m,
then its monotonicity and (9), to obtain (4).

This DOES NOT compare the old and new expectations of 1-a^d,
J_L/L(b), or log[L(b)/V]. Those functions lack decomposition (8).
The bound uses the larger logarithmic Jensen gap.

## 6. Weighted budgets from the same selected coupling

Set T=integral L drho,
c_1=(1/2)integral L d(gamma_-+gamma_+), and
T_old=integral L d(b_#pi_old). Concavity and convex order tested with
-L give c_1<=T<=T_old. For positive mass, use the probability
L(b)dpi/T and convexity of a->a^d:

    integral L dE_pi =T-integral L(b)a^d dpi
      <=T[1-(c_1/T)^d]
      <=T_old[1-(c_1/T_old)^d]
      <=d(T_old-c_1).                                    (10)

The middle inequality uses that T-c_1^d/T^(d-1) is increasing for
T>=c_1>0; for d=1 it is T-c_1 exactly. Zero mass is treated separately.

More generally for 0<p<=1 define T_p,c_p,T_p,old by replacing L with
L^p above. Since L^p is concave, its negative admits a finite global
convex extension using the tangent continuation of -t^p below ell/2
and the maximum over A_i. Thus c_p<=T_p<=T_p,old. Concavity of the
p-th power gives V^p>=mean(L_-^p,L_+^p). Weighted Jensen for the
probability L(b)^p dpi/T_p and the power (a^p)^(d/p) yields

    integral L^p dE_pi
      <=T_p[1-(c_p/T_p)^(d/p)]
      <=T_p,old[1-(c_p/T_p,old)^(d/p)]
      <=(d/p)(T_p,old-c_p).                              (11)

The logarithmic bound is also its p-down-to-zero limit, but Section 5
proved that bound directly, so no limiting interchange is required.

## 7. Normal, parity, and source marks

The final constraints use original coordinates, fixed conditional
marginals, the actual support graph, continuous tuple discount a^d,
and countable domination and convex-order tests. The established
measurable-assembly theorem selects them over normal labels. No
measurable face basis, density representative, or roof enumeration
is needed in the final constraints.

Sum over at most 2^n original parity classes at each normal. The total
laws obey

    D_tot<=2^n omega,
    rho_tot=D_tot+E_tot,
    (rho_tot-2^n omega)_+<=E_tot.                          (12)

The measure E_tot retains actual new midpoint, normal, and parity
labels. Additional source marks can be reconstructed through the
old-to-new midpoint martingale and conditional endpoint sampling.
This preserves the mark and its conditional midpoint MEAN. It may
change the individual endpoint distributions conditioned on that mark.
Consequently the entropy comparison is per normal/parity, where the
endpoint marginals are fixed; no old-versus-new arbitrary-source-mark
entropy comparison is asserted.

Let m_tot be the total coupling mass and Delta_old,tot the sum and
normal integral of old logarithmic gaps. The function

    b(m,Delta)=m[1-exp(-d Delta/m)]

is concave and positively homogeneous for m>0, Delta>=0, with value
zero at (0,0). Equivalently apply Jensen to the union of all couplings.
Thus for m_tot>0,

    E_tot(total)
      <=m_tot[1-exp(-d Delta_old,tot/m_tot)]
      <=d Delta_old,tot.                                 (13)

The zero-total-mass case is trivial. Only the baseline in (12) carries
the parity factor. The error acquires no extra factor 2^n.

## 8. Scope and the remaining interface

Old L-Jensen contact makes a=1 old-almost everywhere. It does not make
its logarithmic gap zero unless the endpoint L values also agree.
The separate contact-constrained theorem can therefore be sharper
than simply applying (4). The present theorem always retains the
stronger exact coupling constraint (2).

The floor coefficient has been removed from the error payment. This
does not show that the actual physical surface entropy vanishes or
is small enough for OC. A sequence with L approaching zero still needs
control of its old logarithmic gap and an independent limiting argument.
No passage through a singular denominator is claimed here.

## 9. Exact sharpness of the one-parity nonlinear tradeoff

Take n=1 and the same d-dimensional cube K at integer bases -1,0,1,
with canonical body [-1,1] times K. Fix a facet normal and let F be
that facet, of surface mass m>0. For d=1 use the corresponding
endpoint atom and m=1. Take H=1 and

    L(z,x)=1+b-b|z|,             b>0.

This is a positive finite concave minimum on the canonical body. Let
gamma_- be the full uniform face law at base -1 and gamma_+ the same
law at base 1. Both are dominated by omega because L=1 at the two
endpoint bases. They share one integer parity class. The old coupling
pairs identical continuous coordinates, producing the uniform face
law of mass m at base zero.

Every admissible endpoint tuple has

    L_-=L_+=1,       L_mid=1+b,
    a=(1+b)^(-1),   delta_log=log(1+b).

The old midpoint law rho_old already maximizes the quadratic physical
midpoint objective among all fixed-marginal couplings. Indeed
write X,Y here for the CONTINUOUS endpoint coordinates; the output
base is constantly zero and contributes nothing to this quadratic.

    E[|(X+Y)/2|^2]
      =E|X|^2-(1/4)E|X-Y|^2
      <=E|X|^2.

Both marginals have the same continuous law. If a feasible midpoint
law dominates rho_old in convex order, the reverse quadratic inequality
forces X=Y almost surely. Thus rho=rho_old; there is no better
convex-order repair hidden in this example. In d=1 the sole endpoint
pair gives the same conclusion directly.

The actual target reference at base zero has density (1+b)^(-d)
relative to rho_old. Consequently

    E_pi=(1-(1+b)^(-d))rho_old,
    (rho-omega)_+=E_pi,
    Delta_old=m log(1+b),
    E_pi(total)=m[1-exp(-d Delta_old/m)].

All inequalities in the logarithmic nonlinear bound are equalities.
The L^p nonlinear inequalities are likewise equalities, since all
endpoint values and all midpoint values are constant. This proves
sharpness for the ONE-PARITY conditional theorem. It does not assert
sharpness for the global 2^n reference after different parity classes
are summed, nor identify this auxiliary tradeoff with an OC payment.

## 10. Affine-weighted relative-entropy payment

The SAME selected coupling from (1)-(2) has a more directional family
of scale-free error bounds. Let q be any positive affine physical
function on C, and define

    F_q(w)=q(w) log[q(w)/L(w)].

This is convex on C. One direct global-test justification is the
relative-entropy variational formula

    q log(q/L)=sup_(t in R) [q t-L exp(t-1)].

The maximizing t is 1+log(q/L). On compact C its values lie in a
finite interval [a,b]. Hence the globally finite convex function

    max_i sup_(a<=t<=b) [q(w)t-A_i(w)exp(t-1)]             (16)

agrees with F_q on C: each fixed-i,t expression is affine in w; all
restricted expressions are at most F_q there; an active A_i=L and
the actual maximizing t give equality. No positivity of q or A_i
outside C is required for this finite extension.

At a tuple write q_0=q(b)=(q_-+q_+)/2 and set

    delta_q=[F_q(w_-)+F_q(w_+)]/2-F_q(b),
    p_-=q_-/(2q_0),         p_+=q_+/(2q_0),
    s_-=L_-/(2V),           s_+=L_+/(2V).

Both p and s are probability vectors. Direct expansion gives the
EXACT identity

    delta_q/q_0=log[L(b)/V]+KL(p||s).                    (17)

Here KL(p||s)=sum p_i log(p_i/s_i)>=0. Its elementary nonnegativity
follows from log x<=x-1, applied to s_i/p_i and summed with weights
p_i; all values are positive in the present case. Consequently

    delta_q>=-q_0 log a>=0,
    q_0(1-a^d)
       <=q_0[1-exp(-d delta_q/q_0)].                     (18)

Equality in the first inequality holds exactly when
q_-/L_-=q_+/L_+. No relation between these ratios is assumed.

The total q-weighted mass is FIXED by affine moments:

    T_q=integral q drho
       =(1/2) integral q d(gamma_-+gamma_+).

The integrated tuple gap is

    Delta_q(pi)
       =(1/2) integral F_q d(gamma_-+gamma_+)
                    -integral F_q drho.

Equation (1), tested with (16), gives
Delta_q(pi)<=Delta_q(pi_old). Jensen applied to the probability
q(b)dpi/T_q in (18) therefore yields the simultaneous bound

    integral q dE_pi
      <=T_q[1-exp(-d Delta_q(pi)/T_q)]
      <=T_q[1-exp(-d Delta_q(pi_old)/T_q)]
      <=d Delta_q(pi_old).                              (19)

This strengthens the constant-q logarithmic bound by retaining affine
physical weights. No new coupling has to be selected for each q;
full convex order of the already selected law supplies ALL tests (16).

The statement extends to nonnegative affine q on C, with 0 log 0=0.
Apply the proof to q+epsilon. The functions
(q+epsilon)log[(q+epsilon)/L] converge uniformly on compact C to F_q,
because t log t is continuous at zero and log L is bounded. Thus
all integrals and the inequalities pass to the limit. If T_q=0,
nonnegativity gives q=0 endpoint- and midpoint-almost everywhere,
so both sides of the linear bound in (19) are zero; the nonlinear
bound is interpreted as zero. If T_q>0 its displayed formula passes
by continuity. Equation (17) also holds directly when some p_i=0,
using 0 log 0=0; where q_0=0 both endpoint q values and delta_q vanish.

One MUST NOT replace q by an arbitrary positive-part hinge. Affineness
supplies both q_0=(q_-+q_+)/2 and the fixed T_q. Moreover the perspective
function's derivative with respect to q can be negative, so composing
it with a convex hinge does not automatically preserve convexity.
Positive affine support-height functions may be used only with their
actual orientation and sign explicitly checked.
